newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal, Indonesia seek new tack on Timor.
newsitem.headline: Portugal, Indonesia seek new tack on Timor.

text.p: Portugal and Indonesia have agreed a new approach to talks on East Timor aimed at injecting fresh impetus into the diplomatic search for an accord over the disputed territory, Portuguese radio reported on Friday.

Portugal's Foreign Minister Jaime Gama and his Indonesian counterpart Ali Alatas, who are meeting in New York, were quoted as saying that the new formula would involve more frequent contacts, but at ambassadorial level.

Little progress has been made since Timor's former colonial ruler and Indonesia, which bloodily annexed the territory in 1976, began to hold twice-yearly talks under the auspices of the United Nations.
The international community never recognised the Indonesian takeover and the U.N. still regards Portugal as the administering power.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, who opened the latest round of discussions on Thursday, appointed a special envoy, Jamsheed Marker of Pakistan, earlier this year to help break the deadlock over the future of the territory, where a group of anti-Indonesia guerrillas remains active.

Alatas told TSF radio that the plan called for the two countries to meet more often but at ambassadorial level. He said that the meetings could start next month and would be secret, out of the glare of publicity.
"They will be confidential. Ministers will meet only when and if necessary," Alatas said.
Gama said that the intention was to include Timorese representatives, although it was not clear whether all sectors of the divided resistance movement to Indonesian rule would be invited.
Alatas confirmed that the range of participants would be extended. "We will slightly expand and make the composition a bit bigger," he said without giving details.
Portugal, which accuses Indonesia of human rights abuses in the territory, says that East Timor must be decolonized and its inhabitants allowed to determine their own future.
Jakarta argues that the territory was decolonized when the Portuguese left and that its people opted for integration with Indonesia.
